title: ‘Too early’ to determine impact of US blockade on Iran, with Tehran defiant
summary:
The US blockade of Iranian ports is having a crippling effect on the economy, but Tehran insists its economy can survive.
Share ‘Too early’ to determine impact of US blockade on Iran, with Tehran defiant on social mediaTehran, Iran – Iran’s economy is expected to contract further due to the ongoing blockade of its ports by the United States, inflicting pain on tens of millions of Iranians.
The US believes its naval blockade on Iran, overland trade disruptions and sanctions – part of its maximum pressure campaign on Tehran – are working.
Strikes on US interests in the region this week, including radar systems in Bahrain, have been viewed as a defiant response to the US military and economic pressure.
Tehran-based economist Peyman Molavi said if current conditions persist, Iran’s inflation could rise considerably over the coming months.

title: Even His Own Officials Don’t Think Trump’s China Trip Will Lead to Progress on AI
summary:
Ahead of President Donald Trump’s meeting with Xi Jinping on Thursday, administration officials privately tell Inner Loop they see little room for progress in alleviating AI safety and espionage concerns.
In the US, Trump administration officials and tech leaders have been most worried about AI models becoming autonomous and misaligned, where they can operate beyond the bounds of human oversight.
But in China, government officials are widely understood to be more concerned about advanced open-weight models being used by critics and dissidents inside the country to undermine the Chinese Communist Party, officials say.
Suspicions about mutual espionage have also exacerbated the distrust on any AI-related negotiations, officials tell Inner Loop.
China has viewed the US as trying to stymie its AI development—and that was even before the Nvidia scandal.

title: Ukraine says letting private defense companies buy and operate air defense systems is paying off
summary:
Ukraine has given some private defense companies the ability to defend themselves with independently purchased air-defense capabilities.
"It also makes it possible to rapidly scale up air defense capabilities without placing an additional burden on the air defense of the Defence Forces of Ukraine," it added.
Companies can purchase approved air defense weapons, including uncrewed systems, surface-to-air missile systems, and anti-aircraft artillery.
The companies involved operate the systems under military command and within Ukraine's larger air defense network.
Ukraine's defense ministry said the program has shown growing success in downing Russian threats, which continue to rain down.

title: Prince Harry, after Ukraine trip, warns on threat from Russia
summary:
There appeared to be warnings about President Trump - with Prince Harry saying there was a big separation between what the American public thinks about Ukraine and the administration's attitude.
Prince Harry said he hoped that after the US midterm elections there would be "more American support" for Ukraine.
"Just because there's not drones, bullets, and rockets flying at us, it doesn't mean that we're not at war," said Prince Harry.
Prince Harry had been in Lviv in Ukraine on Saturday and Sunday - and had told the BBC and journalists at events that he thought the "rest of the world will continue to support" Ukraine.
Prince Harry had received an enthusiastic welcome when he visited Lviv in Ukraine at the weekend, meeting Ukrainian competitors taking part in his Invictus Games.

title: Tensions rise over draft climate deal at COP31
summary:
A contentious draft deal has laid bare divisions between delegates from states participating in this year’s United Nations climate COP31 talks in Turkiye.
The 18-page draft “cover decision” published by summit cohost Australia on Monday includes a broad range of demands, including calls for a phaseout of fossil fuels.
The dispute has become one of the main issues being debated at COP31, which ends Friday.
On Tuesday, the kingdom’s delegation at COP31 defended its position on the publication timeline for the IPCC report, saying “Saudi Arabia is not seeking to delay climate science”.
Saudi Arabia “advocates publication timelines that allow sufficient scientific review, transparency and meaningful participation”, the statement said, without explicitly mentioning when Riyadh would like to see the reports published.

title: Trump Says Iran Will ‘Pay A Price’ If There Was DC Dirty Bomb Plot
summary:
Esmaeil Baqaei, a spokesman for Iran's Ministry of Foreign Affairs, called the reports of the dirty bomb plot "baseless allegations."
What Is A Dirty Bomb?
A dirty bomb is a conventional explosive device combined with radioactive material.
It differs from a nuclear bomb because a regular explosive is used rather than creating a nuclear chain reaction.
A dirty bomb could impact several city blocks, whereas a nuclear blast would vaporize much of a city.

title: Japan sends up jets after alleged Russian incursion of its airspace
summary:
Japan says it launched fighter jets and "strongly" protested after two suspected Russian aircraft violated its airspace early on Tuesday.
South Korea also says it deployed fighter jets, while Taiwan says it "responded" to Russian military aircraft detected in their respective air defence identification zones.
The last such incursion was in 2024, when a Russian military patrol plane entered Japanese airspace off Rebun island, Hokkaido.
Taiwan says its military "responded accordingly" after two Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone, also on Tuesday.
South Korea says it sent up jets after an unspecified number of Russian military aircraft entered its air defence identification zone over the Sea of Japan.

title: Ukraine holds peace talks with US, Europe as conflict escalates
summary:
Share Ukraine holds peace talks with US, Europe as conflict escalates on social mediaUkraine has held new talks with United States and European officials on ending the war with Russia, hours before Kyiv’s mayor reported strikes on two bridges in the capital.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described Monday’s online discussions with US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner and European representatives as “not easy”.
But he said participants had agreed to meet in Berlin with the “Coalition of the Willing”, a group of countries supporting Ukraine, as the US and Europe step up peace talks this week.
Witkoff and Kushner later met Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow and said European representatives would join the next round.
Ushakov said Russia had not agreed to expand the talks beyond the existing Russian, Ukrainian and US delegations.

title: Trump announces critical minerals agreements at Quad meeting in Manila
summary:
US President Trump said the deals would prevent ‘coercion by any single foreign supplier’.
United States President Donald Trump says that members of the Quad, a security grouping of the US and three Indo-Pacific countries, have reached agreements aimed at securing supply chains of critical minerals.
Trump met India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi – the other Quad leaders – in the Philippines on Thursday.
During the meeting, Trump said the agreements on critical minerals aimed to prevent “coercion by any single foreign supplier”.
In a statement after the leaders’ meeting, the Quad expressed “grave concerns” about “economic coercion”, including through arbitrary export restrictions.
